target: Automation architecture: Codex automations ↔ .azoth/inbox governed intake flow
summary: Emerging automation pattern: domain-specific automations should stay narrow, while a separate inbox-authority synthesis automation aggregates cross-automation signals and emits only high-signal D32 insights.
evidence: Session design review on 2026-04-18 established two constraints from live automation work: (1) `skill-progression-map` must remain focused on skill improvement/new skill suggestions rather than inbox sending, and (2) future automation-driven inbox writes are still desirable, but only after synthesis. The durable shape is a two-layer model: per-domain automations (skill progression, bug scan, performance audit, etc.) produce narrow findings; one separate synthesis automation reads those outputs, detects repeated or materially important patterns, and only then sends governed insight records to `.azoth/inbox/`. This avoids turning every automation into a direct inbox writer and preserves `/intake` as a high-signal triage layer.
recommended_action: Create a backlog initiative for a dedicated cross-automation insight synthesizer with inbox authority. Scope it to: ingest outputs from other automations, require concrete evidence and recurrence/materiality thresholds, emit D32-compliant inbox records, and keep all other automations default-denied from direct inbox writes unless explicitly approved.
